note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, price, session time and net rule below comes from one page on the Town of Mount Pleasant's website - the Recreation Department's pickleball page - which lists five entries under two headings, Indoor and Outdoor, and prints a count, a two-line address and a paragraph of rules under each. Two of those entries share one address at Park West and publish here as one venue. Where the Town is silent - on surface everywhere, on lighting everywhere except the Park West tennis courts, on parking at every site - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: The Town publishes nothing about parking at any of these four sites. The word does not appear under any of the five entries on its pickleball page, and this site does not fill the gap from a map. What the Town does publish is where things are kept and where you check in. At Park West the outdoor nets come from "the Program Building directly beside the courts", Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., so a first visit outside those hours means arriving with a net of your own. At Miriam Brown Community Center the nets are held in a different building again, the G.M. Darby Building, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the Town does not say how far that is from the courts. Indoors, every gym session begins at a desk: "All players MUST sign in" at Park West Gym and at The Deb Gym at Town Hall, and the Deb Gym is inside the Town's Municipal Complex at 100 Ann Edwards Lane, the address the Town gives for itself at the foot of the page. The Senior Center on Von Kolnitz Road asks non-members for a guest fee before they join in. Restrooms are not mentioned at any of the four, and neither are bus stops, so nothing is claimed about either. The one rule the Town prints about what you carry in is for the gyms: "Only water allowed inside the gym. NO OTHER FOOD OR DRINK ALLOWED."
slots.peak_hours: Mount Pleasant does not say when its courts are busy, but it prints a session for every venue, and at three of the four the session is the only time pickleball exists there. Park West Gym runs Tuesdays and Thursdays, 8:00 am to 12:00 pm, plus eight Sunday mornings the Town lists by date for the autumn of 2026, from September 13 to November 15, 8 a.m. to noon. The Deb Gym at Town Hall runs Mondays 1:00 to 3:00 pm, Wednesdays 9:00 am to 12:00 pm and Fridays 8:00 am to 12:00 pm. The Senior Center's one court is in use Tuesday and Thursday 3:00 to 4:50 pm and Friday 3:00 to 5:50 pm. All of those are weekday daytime windows; the Town schedules no indoor evening at all. The evening belongs to the Park West tennis courts, where "Organized Open Play Group Meets Every Monday, Tuesday & Wednesday 6:00 - 8:00 pm" and a spot must be reserved on the TeamReach app with the code 29466. Those are the four lit courts. Miriam Brown is the mirror image: an open play group every morning of the week, 7:00 to 11:00 am, and then a printed ban - "NO OPEN PICKLEBALL PLAY WHEN THE COMMUNITY CENTER IS OPEN!" - covering Monday to Friday 2:30 to 6:30 pm and Saturday 11:00 am to 3:30 pm from September to May, and Monday to Friday 11:30 am to 3:30 pm from June to August. From September 18 to October 31 the Deb Gym's four courts become two for volleyball season, and on the Park West tennis courts the Town's own pros "do have court priority for lessons", with Monday afternoon closures, 3:30 to 6:30 pm, listed from August 24 to December 7.
slots.surface_condition: The Town names no surface for any court in Mount Pleasant, and this page will not supply one. What it names, precisely, is what each court is drawn on and who puts the net up. Eleven of the nineteen courts are in gymnasiums. The Town's schedule link calls them "Open Play Schedule in Gyms (including Basketball & Badminton)", the Deb Gym gives up two of its four courts to volleyball season each autumn, and Park West Gym closes for voting on November 3, so these are shared floors that become pickleball courts when the nets go up. The Town says as much in its own instruction: "Nets are provided for players to set up", and players should "prepare for breakdown a few minutes prior to end time". Four of the eight outdoor courts are the Park West Tennis Courts, tennis courts first in name and in priority, and the one place the Town states lighting: "4 Courts - Lighted". Nothing is said about how the pickleball lines sit on them. The other four, at Miriam Brown Community Center, are described by a count and a net rule and nothing else; the Town does not say whether they are dedicated courts or lined onto something, and it does not say whether they are lit. Nowhere on the page is there a word about resurfacing, cracks or condition. Lighting, then, is stated for four courts of nineteen, unstated for the other four outdoors, and not a question the Town addresses indoors.
slots.local_scene: Nineteen verified courts across four Town sites, eleven of them indoors, and three of the four sites free in the Town's own words. Mount Pleasant is the first South Carolina city on this site and the first in Charleston County. It is one of seven cities on this site with a verified free court, and the free ones are the big ones: Park West with six gym courts and four lit tennis courts, The Deb Gym at Town Hall with four, Miriam Brown Community Center with four. The fourth site, the Senior Center, has one court and a condition: "Drop-in play is for anyone 50 years and older and is free for members of the Senior Center", a guest fee of $5 for residents and $10 for everyone else, and the line "Nets, balls, and paddles are provided". The Town is one of the few operators on this site that states the age restriction, the guest fee and the equipment provided at a venue in one paragraph. The organised side of the game is written down too. An evening group plays the Park West tennis courts Monday to Wednesday through the TeamReach app. At Miriam Brown the Town names Coach Don Fickling, "a PCI Certified Pickleball Coach", assisted by Jackie Kelly, "USA Pickleball Ambassador", who together "lead Old Blue Truck Pickleball", and it runs clinics at both Miriam Brown and the Deb Gym for ages 18 and up, eight players each, in beginner, intermediate 3.0 to 4.0 and advanced 4.0-plus groups - priced as clinics, $50 for residents and $80 for non-residents, which are lesson prices and not court prices. In April 2026 the Town held the Al Bradshaw-Whittemore Pickleball Classic in Park West Gym, doubles on the Saturday and mixed on the Sunday, $50 a team, round robin, games to 15 win by two, medals by division and no referees, and it asks players to "Join our MPRD DUPR Club so we can report scores". Nothing was refused in Mount Pleasant: every entry on the Town's page carries a count and an address, and all four addresses resolve.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts in one place
best_for.text: Park West has ten of Mount Pleasant's nineteen courts at one address: six in the gym on Tuesday and Thursday mornings and listed autumn Sundays, and four lit tennis courts outside that host the Town's Monday-to-Wednesday evening group. Free on both sides of the door. Nets are provided in the gym and lent from the Program Building on weekdays outside; bring your own after 5:00 p.m.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a free indoor session on a weekday
best_for.text: The Deb Gym at Town Hall has four free indoor courts on three weekday sessions - Monday afternoon, Wednesday and Friday mornings - with nets provided and a sign-in at the door. Plan for two courts rather than four between September 18 and October 31, when the Town gives the floor to volleyball season, and check its closure dates, which include Veterans Day and the day after Thanksgiving.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a game every morning of the week
best_for.text: Miriam Brown Community Center is the one Mount Pleasant venue with a session every day of the week: an open play group from 7:00 to 11:00 am, Monday to Sunday, on four free outdoor courts. Nets come from the G.M. Darby Building on weekdays. The Town prints when not to come in capitals - no open play while the community centre is open, with the hours given by season.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Mount Pleasant have?
faqs.a: We have verified 19 across four Town sites: ten at Park West (six in the gym and four on the lit tennis courts), four at The Deb Gym at Town Hall, four at Miriam Brown Community Center and one at the Senior Center. Eleven are indoor and eight outdoor, on the Town's own Indoor and Outdoor headings. Nothing the Town lists was refused.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: At three of the four venues, yes, in the Town's words: "Drop-in play is free" in the two gyms, and "free and first come, first served" at Miriam Brown and on the Park West tennis courts. The Senior Center is free for its members; non-members pay a guest fee of $5 if they live in Mount Pleasant and $10 if they do not, and play there is for people 50 and older.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Not at the gym sessions or the Senior Center, where nets are provided. Outdoors the Town lends nets on weekdays - from the Program Building at Park West, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and from the G.M. Darby Building at Miriam Brown, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. - and states for Park West that "You must provide your own net if playing outside of business hours." Paddles and balls are yours to bring everywhere except the Senior Center.

faqs.q: Which Mount Pleasant courts have lights?
faqs.a: The four Park West tennis courts, which the Town lists as "4 Courts - Lighted" and which carry its Monday to Wednesday evening group. The Town says nothing about lighting at Miriam Brown's four outdoor courts, so that is recorded as unverified rather than as a no. The eleven indoor courts are in gyms, where the question does not arise.
